record_identity.title: Spokane Transit navigation system routed double-decker bus to low bridge, injuring seven

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Spokane Transit navigation system routed double-decker bus to low bridge, injuring seven
incident_identity.date_basis: Spokesman-Review reporting identifies 18 January 2026 as the collision date.

summary: A Spokane Transit double-decker bus struck a low-clearance railway viaduct after following an onboard computer-aided dispatch and navigation route; seven people were hospitalised with non-life-threatening injuries.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The Spokesman-Review reports that the onboard routing system appears to have directed the bus toward the low bridge. Seven people were taken to hospital, and the driver was cited for negligent driving. The reviewed evidence describes computer-aided dispatch and navigation but does not establish that the routing system used artificial intelligence.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence is a consequential routing and human-oversight failure, but its qualification as an AI-related Incident remains unresolved. VIGIL therefore preserves the evidence and harm without assigning an AI-specific failure mechanism.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case is useful for distinguishing automation and navigation failures from AI failures: admission should depend on evidence of an AI-related system, not on the seriousness of the outcome.
assessment_boundaries: No reviewed source establishes an AI or machine-learning component in the routing system.
Responsibility is not attributed solely to the routing system; police also cited the driver and the investigation was ongoing.
